record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Fix any graph G with three vertices and any k at least 2. Over RCA0, assuming the rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of triples of natural numbers, does it follow that the rainbow Ramsey theorem holds for k-bounded colorings of copies of G inside the Rado graph?

evidence.quote: What about k-bounded colorings of graphs with three vertices in the Rado graph versus k-bounded colorings of triples of natural numbers?
does the rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of copies of G in the Rado graph follow over RCA0

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) The Rado graph R is the unique countable graph that is universal and ultrahomogeneous: every isomorphism between finite induced subgraphs of R extends to an automorphism of R. Equivalently, R is the countable random graph characterized by the extension property.

(b) For a finite graph G, a "copy of G in R" is an induced subgraph of R isomorphic to G. Let Copies(G, R) denote the set of all induced copies of G in R.

(c) For an integer k ≥ 2, a coloring c : X → ω (where X = [ω]^n or X = Copies(G, R)) is called k-bounded if for every color v ∈ ω, |c^{-1}(v)| ≤ k.

(d) A set Y ⊆ X is called rainbow for c if c restricted to Y is injective. The rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of triples of natural numbers, denoted RRT^3_k, is the statement: for every k-bounded coloring c : [ω]^3 → ω, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ω such that c is injective on [H]^3.

(e) The rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of copies of G in the Rado graph, denoted RRT^G_k(R), is the statement: for every k-bounded coloring c : Copies(G, R) → ω, there exists a subgraph R' ⊆ R isomorphic to R such that c is injective on Copies(G, R').

(f) RCA_0 is the standard base theory of reverse mathematics consisting of Recursive Comprehension.

Problem. Let G be any graph on three vertices (so G is one of: the empty graph on three vertices, the graph with exactly one edge, the path P_2, or the triangle K_3), and let k ≥ 2 be an integer. Working over RCA_0, does

    RRT^3_k  ⟹  RRT^G_k(R)?

Determine whether this implication is provable in RCA_0 for every such G and every k ≥ 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is presented as one of a list of open problems on the reverse mathematics of Ramsey theory on the Rado graph. Related results in the area (rainbow Ramsey for pairs and triples, and rainbow Ramsey for ultrahomogeneous structures including the Rado graph) have been studied (Csima–Mileti; Dobrinen and others), but no source located resolves the specific implication RRT^3_k ⟹ RRT^G_k(R) over RCA_0 for arbitrary three-vertex graphs G.

status_evidence.title: The Strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for pairs is strictly weaker than Ramsey's Theorem for pairs over RCA_0.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes baseline reverse-mathematical strength of rainbow Ramsey for pairs but does not address the Rado-graph version for triples.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey Simple Structures
status_evidence.snippet: Certain ultrahomogeneous binary relational structures, such as the Rado graph, are rainbow Ramsey.
status_evidence.claim: Treats rainbow Ramsey for the Rado graph at the combinatorial level, not the reverse-mathematics implication asked here.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for Triples is Strictly Weaker than ACA
status_evidence.snippet: RCA_0 + RRT for 2-bounded colorings of triples does not prove ACA_0.
status_evidence.claim: Pins down strength of RRT for triples of integers but does not relate it to the Rado-graph version.
